html:
French settlers from St Kitts first settled Saint Barthelemy in 1648, sent by the governor of the French Caribbean. The island is dry, rocky and small, with no room for big sugar estates.

The early colony was attacked by the Kalinago and briefly given to the Knights of Malta. Settlers from Normandy and Brittany later made it home, living by fishing, small farms and trade.

Because there were few plantations, the island had far fewer enslaved people than its neighbours, and many families today descend from these French settlers. Their story runs on through the Swedish century and the return to France.
